paper.title: A multi-agent automated research pipeline for wind engineering: Application to neural surrogates for urban wind field prediction
paper.status_en: Manuscript in preparation — not peer reviewed
paper.status_zh: 稿件修改中，未经同行评审
paper.abstract_en: We present a multi-agent automated research pipeline for wind engineering in which LLM-driven agents (planner, code generator, reviewer, controller, executor, monitor and runner) propose surrogate models, implement and smoke-test them, train them on a remote HPC cluster under a locked data and evaluation contract, and review the results to plan the next round, with minimal human intervention. The pipeline is demonstrated on surrogates that predict pedestrian-level urban wind fields from building-height images (UrbanTALES dataset) in three modes: grid, sequential and hybrid; about 800 candidate configurations were trained. On one fixed train/validation/holdout split, the best hybrid-mode candidate, a 6.9-million-parameter anisotropic-kernel U-Net, reached a three-seed median R² of 0.795 versus 0.728 for the reproduced baseline, but remained below results reported for a human-designed two-stage system. The pipeline is proposed as a starting stage for propose–code–evaluate research loops.
paper.abstract_zh: 本文提出风工程多智能体自动化科研流程：大模型智能体提方案、写代码、冒烟测试，在超算上训练并复盘。以城市行人风场代理模型为例比较网格、顺序、混合三种模式，约训练800个配置；在固定划分下最佳模型三种子中位R²为0.795，基线0.728。
